summary: Add tradition-group preset picker to scope page
description:
The scope page (src/app/(app)/settings/page.tsx, nav-labelled Scope) renders 21 traditions as a flat one-at-a-time toggle list, which got tedious as the corpus grew. Add a preset picker above the tradition list that pre-selects texts in broad strokes.

Presets (curated slug-lists — corpus.traditions carries no era/region/family metadata, so grouping is editorial and lives in code), 3 axes / 10 chips, non-exclusive, members overlap freely:
- Era: Ancient / Medieval / Modern (Modern = print-era: renaissance_hermeticism, western_esoteric, finnic)
- Region: Western / Eastern / Near Eastern / Indigenous (egyptian in BOTH Near Eastern and Indigenous, per user)
- Current: Hermetic / Platonic / Abrahamic

Decisions (user, 2026-07-17): egyptian in both region groups; no single-member presets; carry all three axes.

Behavior: chips are an additive filter you build up, NOT a mirror of the rows. Chips are grey until armed; arming one narrows scope to only that group, arming another widens to the union, disarming all reopens the full corpus. Armed state is ephemeral UI — not persisted, not derived from the saved scope; the tradition rows remain the source of truth. Any manual per-tradition/text edit (or solo / Include all) clears every chip so a chip highlight can never contradict row state. Absolute set at tradition granularity, so partial per-text selections don't survive a chip click, by design. Flows through existing setCatalog -> debounced autosave; no new save path. Members absent from the live corpus are filtered out and an all-absent preset drops its chip, so adding/removing a tradition later can't leave a dead button. (Replaced an earlier tri-state design where chips mirrored catalog state — with the corpus open by default every chip read as "on" and narrowing meant clicking off what you didn't want, which was backwards.)

Maintenance: PRESET_AXES is a hand-curated slug list, not algorithmic — a new tradition must be assigned an Era (exactly one) and a Region (at least one) or it appears in no chip. CI guards this: tests assert Era partitions and Region covers the tokens.tradition slug set, so a forgotten assignment fails at build.

Implementation (already built on working tree):
- src/lib/scope-presets.ts — PRESET_AXES data + pure armedMembers (union of armed presets) / scopeFromArmed (union -> catalog scope) helpers
- src/app/(app)/settings/page.tsx — ephemeral armed state, togglePreset handler, picker JSX above the rows; the four manual handlers clear armed
- src/__tests__/scope-presets.test.ts — armedMembers union + scopeFromArmed derivation + integrity (every member slug is a real tradition hue key, Era partitions / Region covers the corpus, no <2-member preset)

Done contract: tsc clean; scope-presets tests pass; /settings compiles and serves 200. Full click-through is behind Clerk auth (user to browser-verify layout).

resolution.note: Preset picker shipped: 3 axes / 10 chips above the tradition list as an additive filter (grey until armed; scope = union of armed presets; none armed = full corpus), ephemeral non-persisted armed state, absolute-set apply through existing autosave. Any manual row edit clears the chips. Era-partition / Region-cover integrity guards keep the curated list honest as traditions are added. tsc clean; preset + existing scope tests pass; /settings serves 200. Layout browser-verify pending (Clerk-gated).
